payloads.summary: Saved image attachments are missing when editing a visit note

content.text: An image uploaded through a visit note saves successfully and appears on the patient's Attachments page, but it is missing when we reopen that note for editing.
On https://dev3.openmrs.org, open a test patient with an active visit.
Add a visit note with a primary diagnosis, note text and one PNG image.
Click Save and close. Confirm the image appears on the patient's Attachments page.
Go to Visits, expand the visit and open Timeline.
Open the saved Visit Note encounter's actions menu and select Edit this encounter.
The note text and diagnosis reload. The Image section contains only Add image, with no saved thumbnail.
Images uploaded through a visit note should remain associated with that encounter and appear when the note is reopened for editing.

Reproduced on dev3 on 16 September 2026 with Tiny Test and the note text "QA attachment test: single PNG upload, 16 September 2026." The single image saved successfully before reopening the note. This is separate from the concurrent-upload failure tracked in ATT-65.

The visit-note form calls createAttachment with the patient UUID and uploaded file. The shared helper sends no encounter UUID, although AttachmentResource.upload accepts an encounter parameter and ComplexObsSaver assigns it to the attachment observation.
The edit form also starts with an empty images array and does not load saved attachments. Linking uploads alone will not populate the edit form.
Pass the saved visit-note encounter UUID when uploading its images.
Load attachments associated with that encounter when editing the note.
Keep saved attachments separate from new uploads so a text edit does not upload existing images again.
Preserve existing patient-level attachments on the Attachments page. Do not infer a note association for older attachments that were saved without one.
Create a note with one image, save it and reopen it: the saved image is visible.
Edit only the note text and save: the existing image remains and is not duplicated.
Add another image while editing and save: both images appear when the note is reopened.
Attachments from other encounters are not shown as belonging to this note.
Related historical work: O3-2618 wired visit-note uploads into the patient Attachments page. It did not specify loading those images when editing the note.

payloads.summary: Capture and surface diagnosis certainty (confirmed / provisional)

content.text: Every diagnosis saved through the visit note form is presumed by fiat: the form provides no certainty control and hardcodes certainty: 'PROVISIONAL' on each diagnosis it saves (createDiagnosis in visit-notes-form.workspace.tsx). The backend stores certainty per encounter diagnosis (enum CONFIRMED / PROVISIONAL), and other writers such as REST clients may set CONFIRMED, but the primary authoring flow cannot.

Nothing displays the field either. The DiagnosisTags styleguide component renders only the diagnosis name and a rank-based color (red for primary, blue for secondary). The encounters table resource fetches certainty into its row model but no component renders it, and the visits widget representation does not fetch it at all.
The distinction between a confirmed and a provisional diagnosis is clinically meaningful, and a field that is neither captured nor displayed cannot carry it.

Add a certainty control to the visit note form so clinicians can mark each diagnosis confirmed or provisional, using the backend's own terms (which also match FHIR's Condition.verificationStatus). Needs design input.
Display certainty wherever diagnosis tags are rendered. Tag color already encodes rank, so options for design review:
A text suffix, for example "Diabetes mellitus (provisional)". Survives colorblindness, screen readers, and printing. Confirmed diagnoses stay unmarked so the common case adds no noise.
An outline (vs. filled) tag treatment for provisional diagnoses.
A tooltip or accessible description only.
Visit note form in esm-patient-notes-app: add the certainty control and stop hardcoding PROVISIONAL.
DiagnosisTags in esm-core's styleguide (separate esm-core PR).
Add certainty to the visits widget representation in esm-patient-chart so visit-level rollups have the data. The encounters table representation already fetches it.

Extend the dedupeDiagnoses helper (added in O3-5822) with specified aggregation rules for duplicates of the same concept across encounters of one visit: identity is the concept UUID or exact non-coded text; rank is the minimum across duplicates (primary if primary in any encounter); certainty is the strongest across duplicates (confirmed if confirmed in any encounter). Document and test both rules. The result is a display-level aggregate: it retains one contributing record's uuid (as a stable key), display, and diagnosis reference, while rank and certainty are aggregates that may not match that record. It must not be treated as an encounter diagnosis.
Visual encoding for certainty on tags, pending design input.
Whether tag length is a concern in dense visit rows with several diagnoses.
Whether existing PROVISIONAL data should be labelled as provisional once display lands, given it was recorded without clinician choice.

payloads.summary: Vitals and biometrics chart view shows a loading spinner and causes layout jump on first switch

content.text: The vitals and biometrics widgets load their chart code lazily, so the first time a user switches from the table view to the chart view, there's a delay while the chart code downloads. During that delay the widget shows a single-line loading indicator, which collapses the card to one row. Widgets below it jump up, then get pushed back down when the chart appears. This is noticeable on slower connections and is disorienting, especially for keyboard users where focusing and activating the switcher happen almost together.

The delay itself is also avoidable in most cases: the chart code could be ready by the time the user actually clicks, since there's a clear signal of intent beforehand (hovering or focusing the switcher).
Hovering over or focusing the table/chart switcher begins preparing the chart view so that, in the common case, clicking it shows the chart with no visible loading state.
If preparation fails, no error toast or unhandled error appears to the user, and switching to the chart view still works (it retries).
When the chart is not yet ready, the loading placeholder matches the height of the final chart view so the card and the widgets below it do not shift.
The loading placeholder remains accessible to screen readers (announced as loading / progress).
Applies to both the vitals widget and the biometrics widget.
Card height is identical in loading state and rendered state.

payloads.summary: Prevent loss of unsaved medication dosage entries when switching dosage modes

content.text: When entering a medication order, switching from structured dosage to free-text dosage clears the entered dose, unit, route, frequency, and patient instructions. Switching back clears the free-text entry. An accidental switch therefore requires clinicians to re-enter their work.
Preserve each mode’s unsaved entries independently while the form remains open. Show only the selected mode’s dosage fields and submit only that mode’s dosage representation.
When a clinician enters a structured dosage (for example: dose, unit, route, frequency, instructions) and then switches to free-text dosage mode, the structured values are lost.
When they switch back, the free-text entry is also lost.
This forces them to re-enter information repeatedly, which slows down medication ordering and increases the risk of data entry errors.
If a save fails, the entered values are not preserved consistently, making retry attempts more frustrating.
Structured dosage details and free-text dosage entries should be preserved independently.
Switching between dosage modes should retain the data already entered in each mode.
Only the fields relevant to the currently selected mode should be visible/active at any given time.
Draft values should be cleared only after a successful save, not when the save fails.

This improves medication order entry efficiency, reduces user frustration, and prevents loss of clinical information during routine prescribing workflows.

content.text: The Start date field in the drug order form is collected from the user but is not included in the Order POST payload. RENEW: posted as a new order with previousOrder, on a freshly created encounter (per backend semantics: a renewal is a new prescription event, not a continuation). The new encounter's encounterDatetime tracks the chosen start date. The form does not inherit dateActivated from the previous order.
REVISE: the user-selected date is sent as dateActivated against the previous order's existing encounter. The date picker enforces a minimum of
computation produces a valid order chain.

Future-dated orders. These are modeled with scheduledDate + urgency ON
DATE, not by setting a future dateActivated (the backend rejects future values during validation). Belongs to #2973.

payloads.summary: "Call" action crashes the page when the API request fails

content.text: The "Call" action in the queue table sends a request to the server to mark a patient as being called. If that request fails for any reason — network problem, server error, missing configuration — the failure is not handled gracefully.
In a development build, the failure produces a full-screen red "Uncaught runtime errors" overlay covering the page; the user has to reload the page to recover.

In a production build (where the dev-only error overlay is disabled), the same failure becomes silent — the Call button click appears to do nothing. The error is only visible in the browser console, which end users do not look at.
Either way, the user gets no proper feedback (toast, snackbar, dialog) about what went wrong. They either see a developer-targeted crash screen or no feedback at all.

A related, separate-but-connected issue: the Call action sends data to the server without first checking that the required values (queue name, ticket number, status) are present. If those values are missing due to misconfiguration, the same silent/crashing failure path is triggered.
Find a queue entry whose status is the default "waiting" status — the Call button only appears for these.

the user sees a clear error message (red toast or snackbar) saying something like "Couldn't call patient — please try again." The page remains usable.

payloads.summary: Prevent open redirect via unvalidated returnToUrl

content.text: A security vulnerability exists where the
query parameter is not properly validated after login, allowing attackers to redirect authenticated users to external malicious sites.
During the post-login process, the application reads the
parameter and navigates the user to the specified location. The current validation only blocks the exact
value, meaning any other input—including full external URLs—is accepted. Since navigation uses
for absolute URLs, this results in unintended redirects to attacker-controlled domains.
Enables phishing attacks immediately after successful login
High risk due to trusted post-login context
Potential compromise of sensitive patient or clinical data
Only internal, trusted routes should be allowed
External or malformed URLs should be rejected
Any URL is accepted and used for navigation
Users can be redirected to external sites after login
is retrieved from query parameters and passed directly to navigation without validation. The navigation mechanism allows absolute URLs, enabling external redirects.
